description: Give guard-aborted eligible workspaces a deterministic, persisted exit by adding a terminal `stuck` phase to the workspace registry and an eager, policy-independent resolution pass in the cleanup loop, so a marker-missing / out-of-root / marker-mismatch entry is resolved once, warned once, and never re-evaluated or re-warned on subsequent ticks or after restart.

tasks.title: Add `stuck` terminal phase to the workspace registry
tasks.spec: specs/runner-workspace-cleanup/spec.md#Stuck-entry resolution is persisted and survives runner restart
tasks.description: Extend `WorkspaceRegistryPhase` with a `"stuck"` value (D1). Add an idempotent `markStuck(workflowRunId)` that transitions `eligible -> stuck` (no-op for already-stuck, returns null when absent), persisted through the existing atomic write-through. Widen `loadFromDisk` validation to accept `"stuck"` so the state round-trips through restart (D1). Fix `markEligible` so it transitions only `active -> eligible` (guard `phase !== "active"`); this keeps an already-eligible entry a no-op AND prevents a redelivered terminal workflow-status event from reviving a `stuck` entry back into the warning loop (D4). Fold in registry unit tests for each transition, the reload round-trip, and the non-revival invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: `markStuck` transitions an eligible entry to stuck, persists it, and returns the updated entry; a second call on an already-stuck entry is a no-op (on-disk file not rewritten); it returns null for an unknown workflowRunId
A stuck entry round-trips through `loadFromDisk`/`reload` and reloads as `stuck` (it is neither silently dropped nor downgraded to eligible)

`markEligible` transitions only `active -> eligible`; calling it on a `stuck` entry leaves the entry stuck and unchanged (a redelivered terminal event cannot revive it); calling it on an already-eligible entry remains a no-op

New registry unit tests cover: eligible->stuck transition + persistence, stuck reload round-trip, `markStuck` idempotency, and `markEligible` non-revival of a stuck entry; existing workspace-registry tests still pass
`npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass for the runner package
tasks.output: packages/runner/src/runtime/workspace-registry.ts (phase type + markStuck + load validation + markEligible guard) with new/updated unit tests under packages/runner/tests/
tasks.notes: This is the data-model foundation for both spec requirements: the `stuck` phase is what makes resolution (req 1) and persisted survival across restart (req 2) possible. `register()` is intentionally left to set `active` on re-materialize (a re-dispatched run reusing a workflowRunId legitimately restarts the entry); do not change that behavior. Per D1 do NOT evict the entry or move the directory — the stuck phase only ends re-evaluation, the on-disk workspace is untouched.

tasks.title: Resolve guard-aborted eligible workspaces in the cleanup loop
tasks.spec: specs/runner-workspace-cleanup/spec.md#Guard-aborted eligible workspaces are resolved, not retried indefinitely
tasks.description: Extract the three pre-delete guards (runnerRoot containment, marker readability, marker workflowRunId match) into a shared private `evaluateGuards(entry)` used by both the resolution path and `safeRemove` (D3). Add an eager, policy-independent resolution pass at the top of `runOnce`, after the empty-eligible early-return and BEFORE the `retentionDisabled && budgetDisabled` early-return: for each eligible entry evaluate the guards, and on refusal warn once + `registry.markStuck` + increment a new `stuckResolved` counter (D2). Add `stuckResolved` to `CleanupLoopResult` and surface it in `runCleanupOnce`'s summary log (`stuck=N`) and its log condition (D5). Keep `safeRemove`'s guard checks as a defensive race backstop and leave its delete-failure path retrying (transient failures are not resolved). Update the loop guard tests to the new resolution semantics and add coverage for disabled-policy resolution and restart persistence (D2). Confirm the manual `RemoveWorkspace` handler still resolves a stuck entry phase-agnostically with no code change (D6).
acceptanceCriteria: `evaluateGuards` is the single source of the path/marker/match checks and is shared by the resolution pass and `safeRemove` (no duplicated guard logic)

A guard refusal for any deterministic reason (path outside runnerRoot, marker missing/unreadable, marker workflowRunId mismatch) transitions the entry to stuck and leaves the workspace directory intact (not deleted, not moved)

On the cleanup tick after an entry is resolved, the loop does not re-enter the removal path for it and does not re-emit the per-entry `refused to remove` warning (exactly one warning observation per stuck entry)
Resolution occurs even when both `retentionDays` and `storageBudgetBytes` are disabled (the policy-independent pass runs before the disabled-policy early-return)

`safeRemove` still removes the directory and deregisters an eligible entry whose guards pass; a `deleteDirectory` failure still leaves the entry eligible for retry on the next tick (transient delete failures are NOT resolved by this change)
`CleanupLoopResult` carries a `stuckResolved` counter; `runCleanupOnce` in host.ts includes `stuck=${result.stuckResolved}` in the summary line and logs whenever `stuckResolved > 0`

The pre-existing test 'after guard abort, directory and entry remain intact for next tick' is updated to assert the stuck resolution (entry present as stuck, not re-warned on tick 2); new specs cover each guard-refusal->stuck case, cross-tick no-retry/no-rewarn, disabled-policy resolution, and restart persistence via a registry reload
The manual `RemoveWorkspace` handler (workspace-removal-handler.ts) requires no change and still resolves a stuck entry via findByWorkspacePath + registry.remove
`npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass for the runner package
tasks.output: packages/runner/src/runtime/cleanup-loop.ts (evaluateGuards + resolution pass + stuckResolved counter), packages/runner/src/runtime/host.ts (summary log surface), packages/runner/tests/cleanup-loop-guards.spec.ts + support/cleanup-loop-fixture.ts (updated/new specs)
tasks.notes: The phase transition is the structural warning de-duplication — do NOT add a separate rate-limiter/log-throttle. In normal operation the resolution pass marks the entry stuck before the retention/budget passes re-list eligible, so `safeRemove`'s guard-refusal branch is only reachable in a marker-deleted-mid-tick race (a rare, single extra warning is acceptable). Per design, persistent `deleteDirectory` failure is explicitly out of scope (would need a retry budget); do not conflate it with deterministic guard refusals.
